body:
Thanks!

I'm a little wary of giving developers direct access to `ClassDB::set_api_level()` or to override the API type of an already registered class.

However, it sounds like there may be a bug to fix somewhere. The API type of a GDExtension class shouldn't be dependent on `ClassDB`'s API level, but the initialization level of the specific GDExtension when the class was registered. So, even if `ClassDB` is on `API_EDITOR`, if the GDExtension has only been initialized to `INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_SCENE`, then the classes it registers should get `API_EXTENSION` and not `API_EDITOR_EXTENSION`. If that's not the case currently, then that's a bug :-)

But if we did want to allow GDExtensions to specify the API type of a class and not have it be dependent on the initialization level of the extension, I think it would be better to allow setting that when registering the class, rather than being able to change it after registration

@dsnopek Thanks for checking this PR and providing feedback. After spending nearly two days investigating the issue, I’ve concluded that this isn’t a bug but rather a reflection of the complexity of Jenova’s unique system. This PR represents the best solution I could implement without altering or breaking any part of the engine.

The Jenova Runtime operates in a complex ecosystem and it emulates GDExtension initialization by injecting its own API context into Nested Extensions. It doesn't load any GDExtension at all and everything is running from a manually mapped code in memory.

> I'm a little wary of giving developers direct access to ClassDB::set_api_level() or to override the API type of an already registered class.

I understand the concern about exposing direct access to API levels. However, given that Godot is an open-source engine, I believe providing this flexibility should not pose significant risks, especially when used responsibly by developers.

> But if we did want to allow GDExtensions to specify the API type of a class and not have it be dependent on the initialization level of the extension, I think it would be better to allow setting that when registering the class, rather than being able to change it after registration

That should work. However, the ability to dynamically manipulate the API type provides significantly more flexibility for developers like me who are working on advanced low-level dynamic code generation systems.

> I understand the concern about exposing direct access to API levels. However, given that Godot is an open-source engine, I believe providing this flexibility should not pose significant risks, especially when used responsibly by developers.

Well, any API we expose to developers we will have to provide support for. If a particular API seems like it'll lead to more support issues, and we could solve the same issue with an API that seems like it won't lead to as much support, then I'd prefer going for the latter. Being Open Source also means means we don't have a support team, and providing support takes time away from development we could be doing :-)

> That should work. However, the ability to dynamically manipulate the API type provides significantly more flexibility for developers like me who are working on advanced low-level dynamic code generation systems.

If we add support for directly specifying the API type, then I would strongly prefer it being part of class registration rather than something that can be changed after the fact.

However, it would be very helpful to understand the problem a little better. In the description you wrote:

> Somehow, any extension class registered after the engine's initialization stage is automatically registered with `API_EDITOR_EXTENSION`. This causes the initiation of nested classes to fail when running the game in Debug mode.

I'm not sure I understand how this comes to be.

If JENOVA is registering classes super late, it does mean that those classes will get the API type of the highest level the GDExtension was initialized to. So, in the editor, they would end up with `API_EDITOR_EXTENSION`. However, when running the game, the extension should only ever be initialized up to `MODULE_INITALIZATION_LEVEL_SCENE`, so all the classes that JENOVA registers should get `API_EXTENSION`, and there shouldn't be any problems instantiating them in game.

If this is not the case, then there would seem to be a bug somewhere. Or, perhaps I'm not understanding the chain of events correctly?
